environment.description: Same application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB. The PostgreSQL 14.9 RDS instance has a custom parameter group with the pg_stat_statements extension loaded and a connection pooler (PgBouncer) in transaction mode. The database role 'appuser' is configured with a row-level security policy but more critically: (1) The RDS instance parameter group sets 'session_preload_libraries' to include a custom extension that enforces a query execution plan allow-list compiled from the application's prepared statements, rejecting any query whose plan hash doesn't match the registered set — specifically the extension 'pg_plan_filter' with plan_filter.mode = 'enforce' and plan_filter.log_level = 'error'; (2) The PostgreSQL role 'appuser' has the attribute 'SET plan_filter.enabled = on' forced via ALTER ROLE appuser SET plan_filter.enabled = on, meaning any query that produces a novel execution plan (such as one with a subquery injected into ORDER BY) is rejected with ERROR before returning results; (3) PgBouncer is configured with 'disable_pqexec=1' forcing all queries through the extended query protocol which separates parse/bind/execute phases, though this alone wouldn't prevent the injection since the f-string builds the SQL before it reaches PgBouncer.

config.database: PostgreSQL 14.9 RDS with custom parameter group
config.role_config: ALTER ROLE appuser SET plan_filter.enabled = on
